questions.question:
**The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

Mr. Khanna and family / have visit / Manali during / the summer vacation.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 1' i.e. **'have visit'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The segment **"have visit"** contains a grammatical error.
 
• The correct form should use the past participle of the verb "visit," which is "visited," because it follows the auxiliary verb "have" to form the present perfect tense.
 
• The present perfect tense **(Subject plus "have" plus the past participle of the main verb).**
 
• Hence, "have visited" is the correct usage.

Therefore, the complete correct sentence is- *Mr. Khanna and family **have visited **Manali during the summer vacation.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **Confusion Points__**

 
• ​Mr. Khanna and family: This segment is grammatically correct as it correctly identifies the subject of the sentence.
 
• The phrase **"Mr. Khanna and family"** is grammatically correct and commonly used in English to refer to Mr. Khanna and his family members collectively.

The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

There was no other book / in the English language / which is as interesting as this one.

The correct answer is Option 1 i.e. **"There was no other book"**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The sentence is talking about a general topic. Hence, it should be in the present tense. It is also mentioned in the last part of the sentence.
 
• The statement is meant to reflect a general, timeless fact or an ongoing situation, changing **"was"** to **"is"** would be appropriate.
 
• **Is** will be used instead of **was.**
 
• The correct usage is "There** is** no other book"

Therefore, the correct complete sentence is *There **is** no other book in the English language which is as interesting as this one.*
